takeaways: Jason ranks seven areas by median home price gains from 2015 to 2025, using closed-sale data. Every one went up.

In dollars: Dayton led ($300,000 to $570,000, about $270,000), followed by Lakeville ($315,000 to $520,000, about $205,000), Prior Lake ($300,000 to $500,000), Apple Valley ($225,000 to $380,000), Burnsville ($220,000 to $370,000), Bloomington ($200,000 to $345,000) and Minneapolis citywide ($230,000 to $315,000, about $85,000).
In percentages: Dayton still led at about 90%, then Bloomington (about 73%), Apple Valley and Burnsville (about 69% each), Prior Lake (about 66%), Lakeville (about 65%) and Minneapolis (about 37%).
Lower-priced entry points grew fastest in percentage terms, while higher-priced suburbs produced bigger dollar gains. Minneapolis's citywide number hides stronger pockets inside the city.
Dayton's jump came from development, infrastructure investment and room for new construction. Jason's takeaway: buying a home that fits your life mattered more than picking the perfect suburb.

faq.q: Which Twin Cities suburb appreciated the most from 2015 to 2025?
faq.a: Dayton, among the seven areas in the video: its median rose from about $300,000 to $570,000, roughly 90%, driven by new development and infrastructure.

faq.q: Did Minneapolis home values go up from 2015 to 2025?
faq.a: Yes, by about 37% citywide (about $230,000 to $315,000), less than the suburbs in the video, though some city neighborhoods did much better.

takeaways: Seven renovations that usually return the least when you sell, according to Jason. Luxury bathrooms: spend $30,000 and you may get back half, especially in an entry-level or mid-level home.
Over-the-top kitchens typically return only about 40% to 50%.
In-ground pools: about $120,000 to install, but they may add only $20,000 to $30,000 at resale in Minnesota.
Four-season porches return about 50%, and home theaters or game rooms often about a third. One client spent $150,000 on a theater that added under $40,000 in value.
Converting the garage to living space can hurt value badly in Minnesota, where many buyers insist on indoor parking. Hot tubs ($15,000 to $20,000 or more) return close to nothing.
Before a big project, ask an agent what it's likely to add in value.

faq.q: Does a pool add value to a home in Minnesota?
faq.a: Not much. Jason estimates an in-ground pool costs about $120,000 but may add only $20,000 to $30,000 at resale.

faq.q: Which home improvements have the worst return on investment?
faq.a: Luxury bathrooms, over-the-top kitchens, pools, four-season porches, home theaters and game rooms, garage conversions and hot tubs, according to the video.

takeaways: Jason's top five Twin Cities golf communities, with prices as of early 2026. 5: TPC Twin Cities in Blaine (Deacon's Walk), the PGA Tour's only Minnesota course, designed by Arnold Palmer and home of the 3M Open, with homes from the mid-$500,000s to just under $1 million.

4: Edinburgh USA in Brooklyn Park, a public course with a Scottish-themed clubhouse, a putting green of about 40,000 square feet and a club membership with a $1,000 one-time fee. Homes, mostly from the 1990s and often over 3,500 square feet, run from the low $400,000s to mid-$500,000s.

3: Bearpath in Eden Prairie, a gated community with a 24-hour guarded entrance and the Upper Midwest's only Jack Nicklaus signature course. Golf membership is about $45,000 to join; homes run about $1 million to $2.5 million or more.
2: Interlachen in Edina, where Bobby Jones won the 1930 U.S. Open. Membership is by invitation, with sponsors required; nearby homes start around $1.5 million, about 15 to 20 minutes from downtown.

1: Hazeltine in Chaska, host of the U.S. Open, PGA Championship and Ryder Cup, with the 2026 KPMG Women's PGA and a second Ryder Cup in 2029. It had about 50 active listings nearby in March 2026, from the high $800,000s to $3 million-plus, with new builds from the low $600,000s just outside.

faq.q: What are the best golf course communities near Minneapolis?
faq.a: Jason ranks Hazeltine in Chaska first, then Interlachen in Edina, Bearpath in Eden Prairie, Edinburgh USA in Brooklyn Park and TPC Twin Cities in Blaine.

faq.q: Is Bearpath in Eden Prairie a gated community?
faq.a: Yes. Bearpath has a 24-hour guarded entrance and a Jack Nicklaus signature golf course. Membership is optional for residents.

takeaways: A tour of Brookshire, a resort-style new development in Lakeville with three single-family home types and townhomes, anchored by a roughly $6 million clubhouse.

The clubhouse has a pool, tennis and basketball courts, a fitness center, a yoga and spin studio, a reservable gathering room with a fireplace, a meeting room for remote workers, EV chargers, a playground and outdoor games.
A model of about 2,400 square feet was priced around $550,000 at the time, with sod, smart-home features and a pond view.

The Jordan model (about 3,000 finished square feet, around $650,000) has a main-floor bedroom and three-quarter bath for guests or a parent, a mudroom, an upstairs loft, laundry and four bedrooms with walk-in closets.

faq.q: Which Lakeville neighborhoods have a clubhouse and pool?
faq.a: Brookshire, a newer development in Lakeville, has a roughly $6 million clubhouse with a pool, fitness center, tennis courts and gathering spaces for residents.

takeaways: A tour of a Pinnacle Family Homes model in the Pheasant Run neighborhood of Lakeville: four bedrooms, three baths, a three-car garage and about 2,700 square feet, priced in the upper $600,000s at the time.
Distinctive touches: a farmhouse exterior, 8-foot garage doors, 8-foot interior doors on the main floor, quartersawn oak cabinets, a brick fireplace with shiplap, ceiling beams and Andersen windows.
The kitchen has an island seating five, a microwave built into the island and a large window over the sink facing a pond and an outlot that won't be built on.

Upstairs are three bedrooms with walk-in closets, a wide hallway, a large laundry room and an owner's suite with a soaking tub. The walkout basement is unfinished; Jason estimates $45,000 to $65,000 to finish it, ideally by the builder so it's covered by warranty.
Builders' on-site reps represent the builder, so buyers benefit from having their own agent on new construction.

faq.q: Do I need my own agent to buy new construction?
faq.a: It helps. The builder's on-site sales reps represent the builder, so your own agent can advocate for you on price, upgrades and terms.

faq.q: Should I have the builder finish my basement?
faq.a: Often it's the most cost-effective option in new construction, Jason says, because the work is covered by the builder's warranty and the finishes match the rest of the house.

takeaways: Shakopee stalled after the 2008 crash, then took off: affordable land drew builders, people followed, and restaurants and hotels followed them. The population grew from about 20,000 in 2000 to nearly 47,000.

The Mystic Lake Amphitheater (about 19,000 seats, run by Live Nation) opens in summer 2026, with acts like Chris Stapleton, Mumford & Sons, Guns N' Roses and Dave Matthews Band, and an expected $138 million a year in economic impact.

Other draws: Valleyfair (its 50th season in 2026, eight roller coasters and a water park), Canterbury Park racing (late May through September), the 140-acre Canterbury Commons development, Mystic Lake Casino Hotel and the Minnesota Renaissance Festival.

Historic downtown has a social district (May through October) where you can carry drinks between participating spots, plus free Rhythm on the Rails concerts. The Landing, a living-history museum, preserves some of Minnesota's earliest settlement.

About 30 to 35 minutes to Minneapolis via Highway 169, with the Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge, more than 100 miles of trails, about 1,100 acres of parks and St. Francis Regional Medical Center. Jason says the city's property tax rate is among the lowest in the seven-county metro.

Early 2026 market: homes in the mid to high $400,000s, about 44 to 53 days on market and close to 100% of list. Nine builders had about 183 new homes for sale across 16 communities, from the mid-$300,000s.

faq.q: Is Shakopee a good place to buy a home?
faq.a: Jason sees strong momentum: new entertainment venues, room to grow, a historic downtown and relatively low property taxes, with homes in the mid to high $400,000s and new construction from the mid-$300,000s in early 2026.

faq.q: What is the Shakopee social district?
faq.a: An area of downtown Shakopee where you can carry a drink from one participating bar or restaurant to another outdoors, from May through October.
